newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel barges lift gently, low sulphur dormant.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel barges lift gently, low sulphur dormant.

text.p: European fuel barges defied the depressive effect of crude's slump on Wednesday and gained value in thin business, traders said.
Business in the ARA area was done early at $82.50 and $82.75 before levels rose to $83/$84. Trades were later heard at $84, $84.50 and $85 a tonne.
"Its going in completely the opposite direction to crude and I honestly don't know why," said one trader, "but it does help with refinery margins."
Traders noted that a refinery upgrade at Shell Rotterdam would provide longer-term support for the barge market.
Shell said on Wednesday it had started its new hydrocracker at the Per+ complex, which will lead to a 40 percent reduction in the output of cracked fuel oil.
While the Per+ plant will not be fully operational until early autumn traders said supplies of fuel oil to the spot market would get thinner from the end of July.
The new unit will cut the Rotterdam refinery's annual fuel oil production by 1.4 million tonnes to 2.1 million tonnes.
Less Russian cracked was on offer, dealers said, with proportionally more straight-run now available.
The early part of the summer export season saw an unsually large flow of cracked material
Low sulphur markets were inactive, with most traders waiting for crude to settle before resuming selling. No prompt material was seen overhanging the market.
